summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of systolic and diastolic heart failure, atrial flutter s/p ablation, diabetes, and obesity was admitted for worsening dyspnea and lethargy after stopping his medications for four days due to financial constraints. He had recently been switched from metoprolol to atenolol, which likely contributed to asymptomatic hypotension in the ED. He was restarted on metoprolol 12.5 mg twice daily and furosemide 40 mg twice daily, with resolution of symptoms and stabilization of vital signs. His warfarin was resumed after a subtherapeutic INR, and diabetes management continued with insulin glargine and lispro. He remained in normal sinus rhythm throughout admission. Discharge was planned after two days with instructions to monitor weight, adhere to a low-salt diet, and follow up with primary care and specialty clinics.
